messages:
alex: Heads-up — we need a short cross-lang plan for OpenTelemetry SDK integration in inference services (Python/Go/Rust). Main goals: low overhead on hot path, consistent resource attributes for dashboarding, sensible sampling/retention. Any quick recommendations?

maria: +1. Start with a minimal schema: root span per request, children for cache_lookup, model_infer, decode. Add attributes: service.name, model.name, model.version, deployment.id, gpu.type, seq_length, token_counts. That gives us good dashboards without per-token spans.

kevin: For exporters, prefer OTLP/gRPC to our collector (TLS). BatchSpanProcessor everywhere — synchronous exporters kill perf. Set batch size and timeout tuned per language.

anya: Python specifics: use opentelemetry-sdk with AsyncBatchSpanProcessor; ensure contextvars-based propagation for asyncio (uvicorn/fastapi). Avoid starting spans inside tight token loops. Example:

```
from opentelemetry import trace
tracer = trace.get_tracer("inference")
with tracer.start_as_current_span("request") as span:
    span.set_attribute("model.name", model_name)
    # call into runtime (no per-token spans)
    result = await model.generate(prompt)
```

Also use OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS env vars so we don't block on config.

jun: Go notes: use go.opentelemetry.io/otel, instrument gRPC with otelgrpc for server/client interop. Propagate context.Context across goroutines and pass it explicitly. Use trace.Tracer and Start(ctx, "model_infer") for children but keep them coarse-grained. Tune BatchSpanProcessor: smaller MaxQueueSize and BatchTimeout for low-latency services.

kevin: Rust: prefer tracing crate + tracing-opentelemetry bridge. tracing gives us zero-cost spans when disabled and lets us attach structured fields cheaply. Convert to OTLP with a nonblocking exporter (tokio task) and batch. Avoid allocating Strings per attribute — use &'static str or intern heavy keys.

maria: Sampling strategy — default 1% head-based sampling is fine for large traffic, but we should implement adaptive sampling: higher sample rate for errors/unusual latency and model rollouts. Mark root span with rollout_id so we can keep more samples for new model variants.

anya: On cache instrumentation: record cache_hit boolean and cache_latency micros as attributes rather than separate heavy spans for each KV operation. If we need distribution histograms, emit metrics (OTel metrics) not spans.

alex: What about semantic conventions? We should standardize attribute keys across langs so dashboards don't require mappings. I'll draft a short spec: model.name, model.variant, model.commit, deployment.region, gpu.family, request.size_tokens, response.size_tokens, kv.cache_hit.

kevin: Also consider pedantic perf checks: add a microbenchmark harness that toggles instrumentation on/off and measures p95. For Go/Python/Rust we should ensure <2% added p95 in normal loads.

jun: Retention/ingestion: do sampling at SDK edge but also tag spans with "retention.hint": "high" for traces we want to keep longer (errors, rollout samples). Collector rules can then override retention TTL.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: New collector config staged to canary tomorrow 10:00 UTC — will enable OTLP/gRPC receiver with TLS and per-tenant rate limits.

anya: One more: automatic resource detection in collector is nice but don't rely on it. Set explicit resource attributes in the SDK so we get model and deployment data at emit-time.

alex: Great. Action items: (1) I will write the attribute spec; (2) maria + kevin will prototype BatchSpanProcessor configs per language; (3) anya + jun will add minimal change to model service to set resource attrs and cache attributes. Keep it minimal and measurable. :thumbsup:

maria: I can own the perf harness for Python.

kevin: I can run the Go + Rust microbench.

jun: I'll coordinate collector canary with infra team.

alex: Thanks team — we'll review next sync.
